annotations.title: What it would take to lose that much

description:
Starts from a loss the reader names and finds the least extreme combination of market moves
        that would cause it on this portfolio, beside the worst each move actually did in
        the record; also each single company on its own. Typical questions: 'What would it
        take to lose 30%?'; 'A third of my portfolio is my employer's stock: what would a
        crash in it take from me?'; 'How bad would markets have to get for me to lose a
        quarter?'. Instead: for what past crises actually did, past_crises. No probability
        is computed: it says how large the moves would be, not how likely. It does not
        recommend, predict or calculate tax.

base.description: Currency code every figure is expressed in: USD, EUR, GBP, CAD… Default USD.
base.title: Base

holdings.description: What is held: {ticker: number}, 1 to 100 holdings. Weights in any scale (60/20/20 or 0.6/0.2/0.2) or money amounts in the base currency (60000/20000/20000): `units` says which; without it, holdings adding up to 1 or 100 are read as percentages, anything else as money, which makes the falls come out in money. Tickers as the exchange lists them (VOO, VWCE.DE, EQQQ.DE, XAW.TO; 'CASH.USD' for cash). Example: {"VTI": 60, "VXUS": 20, "BND": 20}.
holdings.title: Holdings

loss.description: The loss to explain, as a fraction: 0.25 = lose a quarter.
loss.title: Loss

name: reverse_stress

outputSchema.description: The least extreme market moves that would produce the given loss.

_fence.description: What these figures are and are not: descriptive, no forecast, no advice. Repeat its sense when presenting the result.

coverage.description: Share of the portfolio's movement these directions explain.

data.description: Where the prices came from and what was missing or repaired.

as_of.description: Last date of price history used.

missing.description: Tickers with no usable history (left out).

standins.description: Holdings measured through a stand-in with longer history: ticker, proxy, index, from, until, evidence.

line.description: One sentence: what it would take.

moves.description: Per market direction: label, plain wording, shock needed, sensitivity (beta), share of the loss, worst_seen in the record over the same number of days.

target.description: The loss explained, as a negative fraction.

window_days.description: Length of the move considered, in trading days.
